dateline: Hawthorne, CA / Boca Chica, TX — May 2002–Present
heroHeadline: July 16: Starship IFT-13 Set to Launch Tonight as SPCX Stock Dips Below IPO Price
heroSubtitle: 8,837 days since SpaceX founding — The FAA cleared Starship to resume flights on July 13, 2026, closing the IFT-12 mishap investigation (root causes: ascent heat effects and erroneous engine alarm settings) and authorizing IFT-13 (Booster 20 + Ship 40, both V3) to attempt launch at 22:45 UTC tonight from Starbase — the first Starship flight to carry operational V3 Starlink satellites (20 aboard). Falcon 9 kept up a record cadence in the interim: SpaceX passed 84 Falcon-family launches for 2026 (President Gwynne Shotwell now projects ~140-145 for the year), notched its 600th flight-proven-booster launch July 14 (B1080, 638th booster recovery) and a new single-booster reuse record of 36 flights (B1067, July 9), and flew the Transporter-17 rideshare (July 7) carrying the first commercial nuclear-powered satellite. On the financial side, SPCX joined the Nasdaq-100 on July 7 in the fastest index inclusion after an IPO on record, but shares fell below the $135 IPO price for the first time on July 15 (closed $135.27) after peaking at $225.64 in mid-June. SpaceX also filed for FCC approval of up to 100,000 Gen3 Starlink satellites (July 6) and Musk confirmed plans for a retail Starlink Mobile phone service (June 29), while the Starlink constellation grew past 10,750 satellites in orbit.
